name: Mirabell Gardens
description: Formal Baroque gardens around Mirabell Palace, with fountains, statues, and a view of the fortress on the hill.

name: Mozart’s Birthplace
description: The house on Getreidegasse where Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart was born in 1756, now a museum of his early life.

name: Salzburg Residenz
description: The palace of the prince-archbishops who ruled Salzburg, facing a large square with a Baroque fountain.

name: Salzburg Cathedral
description: A Baroque cathedral consecrated in 1628, where Mozart was baptized. The square in front hosts an open-air play each summer.

name: Great Festival Hall
description: The main hall of the Salzburg Festival, the summer festival of opera, drama, and concerts held since 1920.

name: Silent Night Chapel
description: A small memorial chapel in Oberndorf, north of Salzburg, on the site of the church where “Silent Night” was first sung in 1818.

name: Nonnberg Abbey
description: A Benedictine convent on the hill below the fortress, founded in the early 700s and still home to a community of nuns.

name: Paschinger Schlössl
description: A small manor house on the Kapuzinerberg hill where the Austrian writer Stefan Zweig lived from 1919 to 1934.

name: Villa Trapp
description: The villa where the von Trapp family lived before they left Austria in 1938. It is now a hotel.
